What this walkthrough models

The JavaScript simulator follows the current event_loop.cpp, RESP2 parser, and InputBuffer control flow. It does not connect to a running server. Timing, socket delivery, allocation capacity, and seeded data are chosen for teaching, not measured performance.

The diagram is a map of interacting objects, not a straight-line call stack. Parsing happens before receiving; PING/ECHO bypass storage; consuming revisits the buffer; a drained reply rechecks pipeline input. The step timeline is the exact order for the chosen scenario.

Storage results are modeled at the interface boundary. The C++ hash table and AVL internals are summarized rather than reimplemented. The pipeline scenario uses a protocol demo client; the repository CLI waits for one reply per query(). This trace focuses on one connection. The server also handles multiple clients, EINTR, I/O failures, EOF, and accept/read/write budgets.
